quotes.text: It sounds like there's a beautiful lil' choir of baby chicks singing along with me.
It's weird because I did it all in about a month. Maybe it was the mood I was in, I didn't really feel like writing a 'rock' song.

I feel like I'm most satisfied when I can do it myself… Guitar and bass: I'm okay at. Drums: I can scratch my way by. Keyboard: I'm not super good at, but that's fun for me because I don't really know what I'm doing, and maybe something weird will happen, y'know?
[…] all pitch control you dumbasses, get yourself a tape machine
The guitars sound so fucked up […] It's amazing.

[I'm] finding things that I used to think were really cheesy or really lame, like classic rock guitar sounds weird, the effects, I hated it before. But now I think like flanger? I love it; it's great.

I started listening to music a lot when I was a young teenager, then started going to see local bands, then started playing in bands. Since then, I've pretty much just tried to center my life around being able to make music, don't really like anything else as much.

I really like the way a lot of 70's records sound. I like this guy named Joe Meek a lot, he used to some pretty fucked up sounding recordings in the 60's. I think the distortion in my recordings comes from me not really knowing what I'm doing, but in a way I think it makes them better, gives them a little character maybe.

I'll either just go ahead and start tracking, usually with guitar, and write the vocals last. I've been sitting down and writing songs out on the piano or guitar all the way through a lot more now though, and then recording them later.

I made a demo version of what would become my kind of woman around the time I was recording rock and roll night club. I actually wanted to put it on rock and roll night club initially, but never got around to writing lyrics. I liked the demo, even up till I started writing 2, and eventually wrote words to it. It's just some lovey dovey pop song, not really about anything or anyone in particular.

It's a little more personal I guess, all the songs have a pretty literal meaning to me. They'll probably come off pretty vague in meaning to most people, but hopefully people will still be able to connect with them. I recorded it a lot like I did "2", everything was written and recorded in about a month in my room. There's a couple new sounds, some synth, and I sped my vocals up a little here and there.

It's the first song I tried writing all the way through on a synth, I can't really play piano worth shit, so I tried to write one of those choppy bouncy chord harry nilsson songs, except on a weird ass synth patch. I think the lyrics are pretty self-explanatory, I think I was feeling a little burnt out at the time.

We're in a funny zone right now where AI is coming in and getting good at things, fast. Things start feeling paint-by-numbers sometimes. When you have AI bands coming around, and people listening to music without even realising it's AI-generated, we're in a weird place.

I hear about people using AI to even write lyrics a lot nowadays, which is a bit like… give me a fucking break. I think it's about intention. If people want to climb the mountain, I guess you use the tools you can to get up there. I don't know what you're gonna find when you get up there, but hopefully you're happy.

There's a satisfaction I have with this kind of thing, because of how pure and real it feels to me. It's supremely of me. The most important part of art is the human element, I think. Be it good or bad, that's what I want to hear.
